_template: Finding schema — each key finding is saved as FXXX-[topic].md in project-data/findings/
_instructions: Every finding must include all required fields. Optional fields improve traceability.

claim.description: The factual claim in one sentence. Specific, measurable where possible.
claim.example: The European EV charging market will reach EUR 45B by 2030

evidence.description: Source IDs from source-registry.json. Minimum 2 for high-confidence claims.

confidence.description: high: ≥2 independent sources, no conflicts. medium: 1 source or conflicting data resolved. low: single source, proxy estimate, or significant uncertainty.

so_what.description: The implication — what does this finding mean for the project and recommendation?
so_what.example: Market is large enough to justify entry, but growth is decelerating — timing matters

linked_hypotheses.description: Hypothesis IDs this finding supports or contradicts

linked_deliverables.description: Slide IDs, section references, analysis memo IDs that reference this finding

status.description: confirmed: accepted as fact base. needs_validation: used provisionally, flag for verification. contradicted: conflicts with other evidence. superseded: replaced by a newer finding.

_example_finding.claim: The European EV charging market will reach EUR 45B by 2030
_example_finding.so_what: Market is large enough to justify dedicated infrastructure investment, but CAGR is decelerating from 15% to 8% — growth premium window is closing
_example_finding.author: Sara (Research Analyst)
